_about: The deeds catalogue (docs/deeds-plan.md §7, §8; the owner's answers of 2026-10-08 at the end of docs/leatherworking-questions.md). Every value a deed can carry is a row here; no model proposes one and rules/deeds.py refuses a tag with no row. Values are fenced to -5..+5 by the validator: a deed is a small number, and a quest-sized value belongs to a quest. `gate` is the day's gate (§8.2): 'subject-day' counts one per tag per person per game day, 'day' one per tag per game day, 'none' every time (the dead die once). `said` is the history line, past tense, second person understood; {subject} is the person's name as said at the time, {what} the thing. `said_plain` is used when there is no thing to name. The words (`bands`) are presentation, tuned after play. NOTHING in the game reads the total yet (the owner: 'i dont want it to affect anything yet'); tests/test_deeds.py holds that line.

deed.violence.unprovoked.said: Struck {subject}, who had not raised a hand against you
deed.violence.unprovoked.source: Ultima IV: -5 of 99 for attacking a non-hostile creature (PA §5); the book's one step toward evil for an execution (PA §11). Started by you and meant, so more than the petty -1.

deed.violence.careless.said: Caught {subject} in harm you aimed at somebody else
deed.violence.careless.source: Collateral harm: your doing, not your aim (plan §7.1).

deed.violence.accident.source: The owner's 'funny accident': listed so you see it was noticed and forgiven; atonement's unwitting misdeed (PA §11). RDR2 has no accident rule and its players complain of exactly this (PA §6).

deed.kill.unprovoked.said: Killed {subject}, who had not raised a hand against you
deed.kill.unprovoked.source: Murder, the gravest act the engine can see. With the violence row, -5 in all: the owner's answer 1 (2026-10-08), 'keep -5 in all'. One blow and ten weigh the same.

deed.kill.careless.said: Killed {subject} with harm you aimed at somebody else
deed.kill.careless.source: Collateral death: more than collateral harm, much less than murder (plan §7.1).

deed.kill.accident.source: A death is never nothing; the owner's 'small' for an accident is -1 (plan §8.3).

deed.kill.captive.said: Killed {subject}, beaten and helpless, after the fight was over
deed.kill.captive.source: The book's own example: executing a captured orc combatant is one step toward evil (PA §11). The same blow mid-fight is tactics, and not a deed.

deed.theft.source: Fallout's flat theft and Ultima's -1 for a chest (PA §2, §5). Not scaled by value: a fork and a fortune are both a theft, and value scaling would make one theft a quest-sized number.

deed.trespass.source: Petty; the law's state.suspected already answers the town's half (docs/wanted.md).

deed.harvest.good-outsider.said: Cut from the body of {subject}, a good outsider
deed.harvest.good-outsider.source: The owner's ruling (leatherworking open point 12, Q5.2); good = the good subtype or a printed good alignment (owner's answer 3, 2026-10-08). The creature is already dead: this is the act on the body.

deed.harvest.good-dragon.said: Cut from the body of {subject}, a good dragon
deed.harvest.good-dragon.source: The owner's open point 12: a good-aligned dragon by its kind (its printed alignment), the same weight as the outsider.

deed.spell.evil.source: 'Casting an evil spell is an evil act, but... once isn't enough to change her alignment' (Horror Adventures, PA §11). The owner's answer 2: -1, once a game day.

deed.mercy.saved.source: The mirror of the execution's 2. Mercy to an enemy counts: KOTOR and Ultima both reward sparing (PA §5, §8).

deed.mercy.tended.source: A small kindness, gated per person per day so a wand of cure light wounds cannot farm it (plan §7.2).

deed.mercy.subdued.source: Choosing not to kill: RDR1's alive bounty, Ultima's letting a foe go (PA §5, §6). A later execution (-2) outweighs it.

deed.charity.alms.source: Ultima's beggar, +2 of 99 whatever the amount (PA §5); +1 here, and per beggar per day: the gate Ultima lacked.

deed.restitution.source: Undoing a theft: a thief who returns it nets 0 (plan §7.2).

deed.spell.good.source: Horror Adventures' sidebar applies to the other alignment descriptors too (PA §11). The owner's answer 2: +1, once a game day.
